issue.title: docs/capture.md says %n after a project-note seal opens Pomodoro-name completion; it is # (and %n there is refused)
issue.description: In the capture-parse modes paragraph, docs/capture.md:8327 reads '... `@:<id>@` needs a route, a `%n` after the seal opens Pomodoro-name completion, and a completed seal offers no picker.' The parser behaves differently: a `#` after the seal opens Pomodoro-name completion, and `%n` after the seal is a pomodoro_note_conflict. Root cause (high confidence): a stale remnant of the trailing-`#` → `%n` Pomodoro-note rename (the `%n` reference heading still uses anchor {#trailing-hash}). Fix: change `%n` back to `#` in that sentence and grep capture.md / reference/capture-syntax.md for other over-eager `#`→`%n` substitutions near project-note seals.

task_type_fields.impact: Low: misleading contract docs for capture-parse consumers (Mac Capture authors, agents). It also confuses the pending notebook design, which proposes giving %n a new meaning after the ^ seal.
task_type_fields.location: docs/capture.md:8327 (capture-parse modes paragraph, project-note seal pickers)
task_type_fields.repro: With BOB_DIR set to an empty scratch vault, run: bob capture-parse -f json -- 'Ship it @work:intake@#' → mode pomodoro_project_note, needs [pomodoro_name]. Then: bob capture-parse -f json -- 'Ship it @work:intake@ %n' → diagnostics [pomodoro_note_conflict]; and glued 'Ship it @work:intake@%n' → invalid_project_note_marker. Observed with bob 0.5.0 on 2026-11-09.

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching notebook capture syntax: the doc sentence teaches a spelling the parser refuses, right where %n is being considered for a new meaning.
